feedback.end: Although humans have existed for 300,000 years, we actually evolved from ape-like creatures that existed millions of years ago.

instruction.text: Select the picture of a forest.

feedback.end: The original ape-like ancestors of humans lived in forests. This meant that they were adapted for this environment.

instruction.text: How did this ape-like creature walk in the forest?

feedback.end: The biggest difference between humans and their earliest ancestor is that these creatures walked on four limbs. This also helped them to climb trees in the forest!

instruction.text: Eventually, the ape-like creature evolved into a new animal. Drag the labels to the correct features.

atoms.b: Over time, the original ape-like creature began to live in savannahs with open space rather than ((++forests oceans)). They no longer needed to climb, so they started to walk on ((++two six)) legs instead of four.

As a result, their legs became stronger and ((++longer shorter)). In this new environment, these creatures spent more time outside hunting and foraging, evolving to have ((++less more)) hair so they would not overheat.

instruction.text: Select the skull with the biggest brain.

feedback.end: As time went on, the creatures kept evolving, and their brains got bigger. They became more intelligent and began to resemble the humans of today.

instruction.text: What did these bigger brains allow the first humans to do?

hint.text: More than one answer can be correct.

atoms.b: As humans continued to ((++develop lose)) their minds and bodies, they became more intelligent and advanced, eventually ((++evolving dying)) into modern humans.
